## Functional identification

The 372-aa sequence is **strongly consistent with RlmN**, a bacterial **radical-SAM, dual-specificity RNA methyltransferase** (EC 2.1.1.192). It matches reviewed RlmN proteins over nearly its full length (61.7–64.6% identity; 95.7–97.6% query coverage) and contains the RlmN N-terminal domain and Radical-SAM domain.

**Catalytic activity:** RlmN methylates the **C2 position of adenine** in both 23S rRNA (A2503) and tRNA (A37), producing **2-methyladenosine (m²A)**.

Simplified reaction:

**RNA-adenosine + SAM + reducing equivalents → RNA-2-methyladenosine + reaction by-products**

The detailed annotated reaction uses two SAM molecules and produces 5′-deoxyadenosine and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, among other products. RlmN uses a **[4Fe–4S] cluster** and radical-SAM chemistry.

Close homolog annotations place RlmN in the bacterial cytoplasm and associate its 23S rRNA modification with ribosomal proofreading. These are homology-based annotations for the supplied sequence; its exact substrate activity has not been experimentally tested here.
